newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada says buys 6 mln Clyde shares.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada says buys 6 mln Clyde shares.

text.p: Gulf Canada said on Tuesday that it had bought a further six million shares in bid target Clyde Petroleum Plc in the market in morning trading, boosting its stake in Clyde to 29.3 percent.

Speaking to journalists on a conference call, Gulf Canada advisor Nigel Meek of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Gulf had bought shares from a number of institutional investors on Tuesday, but he declined to confirm whther PDFM, which owns around 14 percent of the company, was one of them.

If PDFM had sold more than one percent of the company it must make a stock exchange announcement before midday on Wednesday, Meek said. Fund Manager CIN said on Tuesday that it had sold around 13 million Clyde shares.
Meek added that "the market has accepted that there is not going to be a (rival) candidate" for Clyde.
Gulf Canada president and chief executive officer J.P. Bryan again warned shareholders that they risked a sharp fall in the value of their holdings if Gulf's bid failed.
"It could be a considerable wallop for investors if this deal should fail," said Bryan, who said the share price could fall back to the 80 pence level from Gulf's 120 pence per share offer price.
Bryan said Gulf had a "two-year window of opportunity" to turn Clyde around before the acquisition would become dilutive for Gulf Canada shareholders.
He declined to say whether Gulf, which is now Clyde's largest shareholder, would retain its stake if it failed to win the 50 percent needed to take control of Clyde.
"Our plans are to acquire the whole company. That would be a decision we'd have to make after the fact," Bryan said.
In a letter to its shareholders on Wednesday Clyde repeated its view that Gulf Canada's offer "seriously undervalues Clyde" and again advised shareholders to reject it.

"Clyde's business has never been in better shape," chairman Malcolm Gourlay said. "We have a bright future and can deliver greater value than Gulf Canada's offer by providing substantial returns through a rising share price and sustainable progressive dividends."
